code.originalText: Six-week review: phlebotomy, drinking, mood, blood pressure and liver imaging

text.paragraph: Six-week review: phlebotomy, drinking, mood and liver MRI. [S]

Mr. Hemingway returns six weeks after intake. He has had three weekly phlebotomies without dizziness, and the fourth is planned after today's blood tests. His MRI this morning has been reported. He is drinking three or four drinks a day, all in the evening, with naltrexone daily; his AUDIT-C for the past month is 7. He has had no tremor or sweats. His mood is a little better but he still wakes early and finds it hard to start writing; his PHQ-9 is 13. Sertraline 50 mg causes no side effects. Home blood pressure averages 136/84. Headaches are about twice a week. His guns remain at the club. The echocardiogram ordered at intake has not been scheduled yet. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1955-04-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 138/86, pulse 80; weight 96.2 kg
Liver edge just palpable, smooth; no spleen felt
Engaged; mood low but brighter; no psychotic features
Alcohol use disorder, severe; heavy daily drinking for most of his adult life; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding of DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder (seven criteria); person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Raised transferrin saturation and ferritin found on routine intake tests, cause not yet known (heavy drinking, liver disease or iron overload)
S — Synthetic presenting finding; superseded when HFE testing gave the diagnosis.
Hereditary hemochromatosis, HFE C282Y homozygous, with iron overload (ferritin over 1,000 ng/mL) and no advanced liver fibrosis on imaging
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. Whether he had hemochromatosis is disputed (CLM-0013); the modern diagnosis is not offered as proof of it.
Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate; Mood Disorder Questionnaire negative and no history of mania or hypomania
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; not a claim about his real mood. The roster's bipolar disorder lead is disputed (CLM-0014) and is not used.
Essential hypertension, stage 2, with heavy drinking contributing
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed by home readings.

Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, slowed thinking and forgetfulness) after repeated head injuries, most recently a concussion with a skull fracture a year ago; chronic traumatic encephalopathy is not diagnosed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented head injuries; alcohol and depression also affect the symptoms.
S — Synthetic finding on diabetes screening; iron overload and alcohol both raise the risk of diabetes.

value.displayName: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate

list.item:
Hereditary hemochromatosis on weekly phlebotomy (E83.110). MRI shows a raised liver iron concentration with stiffness in keeping with mild fibrosis, without advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, so a liver biopsy is not needed and liver cancer surveillance is not indicated. Ferritin is falling as expected and hemoglobin is well above the hold threshold. [S]
Continue weekly phlebotomy; ferritin about every ten sessions.
No liver cancer surveillance; fibrosis to be reassessed after iron removal.

Alcohol use disorder, severe, on naltrexone (F10.20). Down to three or four drinks a day. After seeing that his liver already has early scarring from iron and alcohol, he decided to stop drinking altogether within the month, coming down by one drink a week rather than stopping suddenly. Liver tests are close to normal on naltrexone. [S]
Continue naltrexone and thiamine.
Step down by about one drink every week or so to none; call for tremor, sweating, racing heart, confusion or seeing things.
Offered a mutual-help group or an alcohol counselor; he prefers to work on it in his weekly therapy.

Depression on sertraline (F32.1). PHQ-9 16 to 13 after six weeks: a partial response. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or wishes to be dead; firearms remain off-site; the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone. [S]
Increase sertraline to 100 mg daily.
Continue weekly psychotherapy.

Hypertension (I10). Home average 136/84, above the target of 130/80, and still falling as he drinks less. He would rather wait one more interval before a higher dose. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg; increase at the next visit if home readings stay above target.
Echocardiogram to be scheduled.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis: 2011 practice guideline by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2011); ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (2019); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Major Depressive Disorder (2022); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Weekly phlebotomy. Fourteen-week review in eight weeks with blood count, ferritin, liver tests, PHQ-9 and AUDIT-C. Weekly psychotherapy. Next scheduled visit 1955-06-08: fourteen-week review: phlebotomy, the decision to stop drinking, mood and blood pressure. [S]
